title: Evaluating Sources of High-Purity Synthetic Crystals for Use as K-Ratio Standards: Examples from P, Ca, Ti, and Pb
content: It has become increasingly clear that many of the widely-available primary standards used for calibration of chemical microanalysis measurements are inadequate: there are impurities, heterogeneities, and inter-grain compositional variations; the original sources are limited and some standards are now discontinued; and in some cases there are multiple reported compositions for a single standard or source locality. These discrepancies in calibration standards are preventing interlaboratory comparability and traceability of measurement results. Given technological developments in instrumentation and software for high-precision quantitative analysis, the uncertainty in the actual composition of the primary standards is often the largest source of analytical error in the measurement routine.
